messages:
Maya: Heads up — Acme asked for a permanent per-org routing override so their traffic ALWAYS goes to their Dedicated pool even when capacity is low. They proposed a header-based override from their side: `X-Redwood-Route: dedicated-acme`. Should we allow this or force an allowlist flow?
Raj: We already support header-based routing in the gateway, but it's gated by org config today. What are the main risks if we open this up?
Olivia: Spoofing and audit gaps. Also SLO impact: org-level pins can saturate a Dedicated pool and hurt other tenants if we don't enforce quotas.
Alex: I'm +1 for allowing under strict controls: require a signed header (HMAC) tied to the org API key, and enforce per-org quotas and fallback policies. Must be enterprise-only.
Maya: Can we implement HMAC quickly? Acme expects something like `X-Redwood-Route` + `X-Redwood-Sig`.
Raj: HMAC is doable. Implementation notes: add `org_overrides` table + in-memory cache for fast lookups. Schema sketch: `org_overrides(org_id, allowed_routes[], sig_required bool, expires_at)`. Lookup on request: if header present, verify mapping + sig.
Olivia: Console needs a UX: a toggle "Allow header overrides" on org settings, a visible allowlist of allowed routes, and an audit panel showing the last 90 days of override events and any fallbacks.
sec-team: Security: HMAC signed header is acceptable. Keys must be in KMS and rotateable. Also add anomaly detection for spikes in override usage and an alert for repeated fallback to hosted.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: routing-service PR #723 queued for staging :rocket: (runs tests)
Alex: Need fallback policy discussion: if Dedicated is full/unhealthy do we reject or fallback to hosted? Contract for Acme says failover to hosted (degraded latency) is ok, but they want to be notified. So default fallback should be to a compatible hosted model, but make fallback behavior configurable per-org.
Raj: Agreed. Also add metrics: `override_route_requests_total`, `override_route_failures_total`, `override_route_fallbacks_total` with `org_id` tag. We'll wire these into Console per-org dashboards.
Maya: Can we require replay protection? Timestamp + small window?
Alex: Yes — include `X-Redwood-Ts` and require `abs(now - ts) < 2m`. Check HMAC over `org_id:route:ts`.
Raj: Quick signing snippet we can publish to docs: 
```
# sign
payload = f"{org_id}:{route}:{ts}"
sig = hmac_sha256(secret, payload)
headers = {
  "X-Redwood-Route": route,
  "X-Redwood-Sig": sig,
  "X-Redwood-Ts": ts
}
```
Olivia: Console mockups: I'll add a config card with: Allow header overrides [toggle], Allowed routes (list), Fallback behavior (dropdown: reject / fallback-hosted / fallback-queue), Audit events link.
sec-team: Also require an administrative approval workflow — toggles default to off and require 2 approvers for turning on for an org. Log approver IDs in audit.
Maya: Action items: Raj + Alex to post PR and API/HMAC spec by EOD tomorrow, Olivia to draft console mock, Sec to propose approval workflow, SRE to add metrics/alerts. I'll loop in acct team and legal for contract text.
Alex: One more: ensure we annotate traces so ops can filter by `override=true` when investigating perf.
Raj: Noted — inject `override=true` into tracing span tags.
Maya: Great. Thanks all. I'll ping legal. :thumbsup:
Olivia: I'll attach the mock in this thread when done.
sec-team: FYI we've requested a quick HMAC threat review, will report back.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: staging run passed for PR #723, promoting to canary.
